key_facts: Randy Gail Sperino was last seen alive on the evening of 9 November 1993 in Granite City, Illinois; her body was found hours later in a nearby field, with blunt force trauma as the cause of death.

DNA evidence from the scene was run against standard law enforcement databases with no matches; in 2025 detectives sent genetic evidence to Othram, which used investigative genetic genealogy to identify a male relative of the killer, leading to Albert "Buddy" Zigler, 70, who confessed and was charged in May of this year.

Madison County detectives used Centerline AI (CentralSquare) to analyse more than 2,000 pages of records, reconstruct timelines and organise witness information; Othram says it has helped solve thousands of cases.

Investigative genetic genealogy is not yet used in the UK; the Home Office is conducting a study on whether to adopt it, and Denise Syndercombe Court notes the UK DNA database gives over a 65% chance of naming a person if any DNA is recovered from a crime scene.
importance_reason: Feature-style report on forensic technology and a single cold case; no direct market or macroeconomic impact.

key_facts: UK CPI inflation rose to 3.5% in the year to September, the highest rate in nearly a year and above the Bank of England's 2% target; the rise was slightly higher than economists had predicted, driven by higher petrol and diesel prices. Core CPI was 2.8% in the 12 months to September 2026, up from 2.6% in the 12 months to August. The Bank of England base rate is 3.75%, after six cuts between August 2024 and June 2026. At its September meeting, Governor Andrew Bailey said energy price volatility made rate rises more likely.

Regular pay (excluding bonuses) grew 3.7% annually in the three months to August, which after inflation means real regular pay grew 0.8% between June and August. Ofgem's price cap rose 4% for household energy bills from 1 October; VAT on household electricity bills was scrapped in October.
